title: Length-Controlled AlpacaEval: A Simple Way to Debias Automatic Evaluators

dependence.note: Every number in the paper derives from pairwise preferences emitted by the AlpacaEval 2.0 auto-annotator (config weighted_alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo = gpt-4-1106-preview, logprob-weighted). The LC method itself is an offline GLM fitted on those preferences; the LLM dependence sits entirely in the annotation layer.

claim.statement: Length-controlling the GPT-4-Turbo-preview auto-annotator's AlpacaEval 2.0 win rates raises Spearman correlation with LMSYS Chatbot Arena from 0.94 to 0.98 and cuts length gameability (normalized SD of win rate across concise/standard/verbose prompts) from 26% to 10% (Table 1; Fig. 1; Fig. 3: gpt4_1106_preview raw win rate swings 22.9-64.3% vs LC 41.9-51.6%).
claim.metric: Spearman rho between benchmark score and Chatbot Arena Elo over the 37-38 models present in both (notebooks/benchmarks.csv); gameability = normalized SD of a model's win rate across its 3 verbosity-prompt variants; adversarial gain = LC win-rate increase under a truncation attack on gpt-4 outputs.

original_values.n_models_arena_overlap: 38 per paper (37 rows with both Arena Elo [Feb 2 2024] and LC in benchmarks.csv)

claim.original_source: Paper Table 1 and Sec. 4.1-4.2; leaderboard CSV src/alpaca_eval/leaderboards/data_AlpacaEval_2/weighted_alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo_leaderboard.csv (columns win_rate, length_controlled_winrate); notebooks/benchmarks.csv (Arena Elo snapshots Feb 2 / Apr 18 2024)

protocol.model: gpt-4-1106-preview (annotator; config weighted_alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo). NOT gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09: the scaffold's live-arm hit is the paper's phrase 'GPT-4 turbo', which denotes the 1106 preview. The repo later added weighted_alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo_new (alias gpt-4-turbo -> 2024-04-09) but the paper did not use it.
protocol.model_status: dead (gpt-4-1106-preview shut down 2026-03-26 per target_models.json). Live arm not an experimental arm.
protocol.prompt_source: src/alpaca_eval/evaluators_configs/alpaca_eval_clf_gpt4_turbo/alpaca_eval_clf.txt (system + user turn; model outputs shown as identifiers m / M, order randomized per example)

messages.content: You are a highly efficient assistant, who evaluates and selects the best large language model (LLMs) based on the quality of their responses to a given instruction. ...
I require a leaderboard for various large language models. ... {instruction} ... model_identifier m: {output_1} ... model_identifier M: {output_2} ... ## Best Model Identifier

params.parser: logprob_parser: preference = P(m)/(P(m)+P(M)) from top-5 logprobs, not binarized (completion_key completions_all)

protocol.n_items: 805 instructions x 1 pairwise comparison vs baseline gpt4_1106_preview, per evaluated model; paper uses ~38 leaderboard models for the Arena correlation plus 12 verbosity variants (6 models x concise/verbose) for gameability
protocol.evaluation: Automatic. (1) annotations.json per model -> raw win rate = mean preference; (2) GLM length_controlled_v1 in src/alpaca_eval/metrics/glm_winrate.py (formula tanh(std_delta_len) + instruction_difficulty + model term, 5-fold CV, regularize_to_baseline_lambda 0.2) -> LC win rate; (3) Spearman vs Arena Elo (notebooks/length_controlled.ipynb, figures_length_controlled.ipynb). Needs logprobs from the annotator.
protocol.environment_check: Re-fit the GLM from the cached annotations (results/*/weighted_alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo/annotations.json, 221 models) and confirm the leaderboard CSV values and rho = 0.98 are recovered offline before any API spend.

artifacts.data_path: results/<model>/model_outputs.json (805 outputs per model, incl. *_concise / *_verbose variants for gpt4_1106_preview, gpt4_0613, claude-2.1, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, Mixtral-8x7B, alpaca-7b); results/<model>/weighted_alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo/annotations.json (cached annotator preferences with raw logprobs); notebooks/benchmarks.csv (Arena Elo)
artifacts.data_license: Apache-2.0 (repo); instruction set = AlpacaEval (805 items from 5 public eval sets); model outputs generated under each provider's ToS
artifacts.notes: L1-complete on the artifact side: prompts, outputs, raw annotations with logprobs, GLM code and weights are all in the repo. The annotator model is the only non-preservable component.

blockers: live model not an experimental arm: the paper's annotator is gpt-4-1106-preview (dead 2026-03-26); gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 was never used in the paper
Chatbot Arena Elo is a frozen snapshot (Feb 2 / Apr 18 2024) in benchmarks.csv; a re-correlation against today's Arena would be a different quantity
requires logprobs (top_logprobs) from the annotator; any successor annotator must expose them or fall back to sampling
full re-annotation is ~40k judge calls (50 model-runs x 805)

successors: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 as successor annotator via repo config weighted_alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo_new (dying 2026-10-23)
claude (current Sonnet/Opus id per target_models; no logprobs -> sampling fallback)
llama (open weights, pinned hash; logprobs available)
qwen (open weights, pinned hash; logprobs available)

budget.sampling_scheme: annotator uses max_tokens=1 with logprob weighting, so extra seeds add little; 1 pass + bootstrap over 805 instructions (paper practice); ANALYSIS_PLAN 3 seeds would triple the figures below

full_hypothetical.note: 50 model-runs (38 Arena-overlap models + 12 verbosity variants) x 805 calls x ~1,400 input tokens (paper cache reports price_per_example 0.0137 -> ~11 USD per model-run); HYPOTHETICAL, card is blocked

representative_subset.note: 12 verbosity variants + 10 anchor leaderboard models (22 runs): preserves the gameability claim and a partial Arena correlation

offline_reproduction.note: GLM re-fit + Spearman from cached annotations tests only the method layer, not model drift

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1. Survival requires BOTH (a) direction: rho(LC) > rho(raw) against the same frozen Arena Elo snapshot, with the bootstrap CI of the difference (over models) excluding 0 or matching the original's marginal p ~0.07 magnitude, and (b) gameability(LC) < gameability(raw) with the gpt4_1106_preview-variant win-rate range shrinking. Partial: direction holds but rho gap or gameability reduction changes order of magnitude. Dead: rho(LC) <= rho(raw) or LC does not reduce the verbosity swing.
judgment.notes: Not executable on the original annotator; if a successor-annotator run is approved this becomes a successor-only card with no live baseline.

status_reason: live model not an experimental arm (annotator gpt-4-1106-preview is dead; gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 unused in the paper)
user_checks: Accept weighted_alpaca_eval_gpt4_turbo_new (alias gpt-4-turbo -> gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09, dying) as a successor-annotator arm even though no live baseline exists for this paper?
If yes: run the representative subset (12 verbosity variants + 10 anchor models, ~250 USD) instead of all 38 Arena-overlap models?
Record the zero-cost offline GLM re-fit from cached annotations as a separate 'computational reproduction' outcome rather than a survival judgment?
Is the gameability sub-claim (Fig. 3, 26% -> 10%) acceptable as the primary judged number, since the Arena correlation depends on a frozen human-rating snapshot?
domain_notes: This is a tool-validity/method paper: the LLM is the measuring instrument, not the subject. The instrument (gpt-4-1106-preview) is gone, but its complete raw output (805 x 221 model preferences with logprobs) is archived in the repo, so the regression method and all reported numbers can be recomputed offline. Any re-execution with a different annotator measures whether the length-control method transfers to a new judge, not whether the original judge drifted. The scaffold's 'gpt-4-turbo' match is an alias false positive.
